body.statement: Let \(C_n\) be any interval satisfying the coverage constraint in \(def:minimax-honest-length\). For every pair \(\Pi_0,\Pi_1\) and target sets \(\mathcal T_0,\mathcal T_1\) satisfying \(def:prior-predictive-pair\), \(E_{\mathbb Q_0}[|C_n|]\ge\Delta(\mathcal T_0,\mathcal T_1)\{1-2\alpha-\|\mathbb Q_0-\mathbb Q_1\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\}_+\).
body.justification: Uniform coverage forces a long interval whenever the observed experiments are close but their ATE sets are separated.
body.gap: Low1997 and CaiLow2004, Theorem 1, establish coverage-to-length inequalities in nonparametric Gaussian models; this lemma states the experiment-level version needed for prior mixtures in the discrete causal model.
body.consumer: The direct confidence-length converse, without reducing interval performance to squared-error risk.
